# Punt ST: Player Targets

**Summary.** Steals are one of the most variable categories in fantasy, so they make a sensible punt and a risky thing to pay for at our 18 October auction. For punt ST, the best target is Ivica Zubac at 10 to 14 USD. Add 1 to 2 USD blocks flyers like Yves Missi and Khaman Maluach late, and keep a waiver list of bigs. The bigs on this list bring FG%, rebounds and blocks. They do not bring points or assists, which the notes call the stable categories, so buy those elsewhere.

## Why steals are a good punt

Steals change a lot from game to game and from season to season. One expert rates them down in his rankings because they are high in variance and low in volume. He says not to rely on them. ([10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=863), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1534))

Even elite steals players can fall to 0.7 or 0.8 steals per game in a season. Steals and FT% are the two categories that change most from year to year. ([09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=794), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1346))

High-variance categories are the better ones to punt. You will still win some of them by surprise in a weekly matchup. Stable, high-volume categories like points and assists are bad to punt. Steals also do not tie closely to either a guard build or a big man build. So you can drop them without breaking either build. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=839))

## Do not pay for steals at the auction

Players whose value depends on steals carry extra risk. At our auction, do not pay extra for a player whose rank rests mainly on steals. If one season of steals goes away, much of what you paid for goes with it. ([10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=863), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=794))

Steals are among the most common categories on the waiver wire. They also cause oddities in standard 9-cat rankings. Before the draft, look at the Yahoo and ESPN ranks of your targets. Mark down anyone ranked high mainly because of steals. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557))

Steals are easy to find on waivers. So you can change your mind in-season without wasting draft money. If a matchup is close in steals, you can add a steals player with FAB. Our limit is 6 acquisitions per week, so keep a few moves free for that. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722))

## Core target: Ivica Zubac

Zubac is the only real draft-day target in this pool. He gives elite FG% and rebounds with few steals and no threes. He takes only about 2.8 free throws per game, so his FT% does little damage. Our league paid 20 USD for him last season. The profile note says experts cap him at about 14 USD. Aim for 10 to 14 USD and let someone else go to 20 USD. ([Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md))

Check two things early. First, whether Carlisle plays Zubac more than 30 minutes, and how the minutes split with Huff. Second, Indiana plays only 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That makes him a trade chip before the 2027-03-04 deadline if your playoff schedule matters more. ([Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md))

## Late flyers at 1 to 2 USD

Yves Missi and Khaman Maluach are last-round blocks flyers that fit punt ST. Missi projects about 1.8 blocks with good FG%. Check that he starts over Derik Queen at 25 or more minutes. Also check his FT%: Yahoo projects 69.4%, but he shot 55.9% last season. Maluach needs to win the center job over Ighodaro and reach the mid 20s in minutes. If he does not, cut him. ([Yves Missi](../profiles/players/yves-missi.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md))

Nikola Vučević went for 17 USD in our league last season. Now he is a bench center behind Wendell Carter Jr. Pay 1 to 2 USD at most, and only as a late flyer or a handcuff for Carter. Watch his minutes under Sean Sweeney, Goga Bitadze's role and Carter's health. ([Nikola Vučević](../profiles/players/nikola-vucevic.md))

Aaron Gordon fits punt ST as a forward with decent FG% and some threes and assists. But he played only 36 and 51 games in the last two seasons, and experts see no upside. Let others draft him. If he goes undrafted, he is a streamer, since Denver has few back-to-backs. ([Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md))

## Waiver watch list

Four punt ST bigs rank outside our 144-player draft pool. Leave them for waivers and track their roles. Brook Lopez brings blocks and threes if he ever gets about 30 minutes. Check whether Isaiah Jackson holds the job. Isaiah Stewart is out with an ankle sprain, and his value depends on Zach Edey missing time. Memphis has a full 4-4-4 playoff schedule, so be ready to bid FAB if Stewart starts. ([Brook Lopez](../profiles/players/brook-lopez.md), [Isaiah Stewart](../profiles/players/isaiah-stewart.md))

Maxime Raynaud has efficient FG% and low turnovers. He had starter minutes over the last two months of last season. Watch his knee, any Sabonis trade or injury news, and his three-point rate. Ryan Kalkbrenner gives blocks and FG% on low volume. He is worth a pickup only if injuries to Diabaté or the other bigs give him a regular role. ([Maxime Raynaud](../profiles/players/maxime-raynaud.md), [Ryan Kalkbrenner](../profiles/players/ryan-kalkbrenner.md))

## What this pool does not cover

These bigs bring FG%, rebounds and blocks. Blocks are also a high-variance category, like steals. Points and assists are the stable, high-volume categories you should not punt. Except for a few assists from Gordon, none of these players bring them. Spend most of your 200 USD on points and assists, and fill the big slots cheaply from this list. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722), [Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md), [Ivica Zubac](../profiles/players/ivica-zubac.md))
